question.leadin: Name these French kings named Louis.
question.text: This Louis, whose wife was Marie Antoinette, was guillotined during the French Revolution.
question.clue: His de facto Finance Minister Jacques Necker published fake statistics in a Compte rendu which hid the cost of funding French participation in the American Revolution, and he unsuccessfully attempted to escape to Montmedy.

swap.leadin: This outspoken critic of the death penalty executed thousands of political opponents during his reign of power on the Committee of Public Safety.
swap.text: Name this "public accuser" who promoted the Cult of the Supreme Being and guillotined [GEE-uh-teen'd] supporters of the monarchy during the "Reign of Terror."
swap.answerHtml: Maximilien Robespierre [“robes”-p’yair] (or Maximilien François Marie Isidore de Robespierre )
swap.clue: This leader promoted the Cult of the Supreme Being and secured power after the death of his former ally Georges Danton.

question.text: This tribe was first united under Clovis I of the Merovingian dynasty. Under Charlemagne, this tribe came to control large portions of western Europe.
question.clue: Fantasia meant "stubbornness" or "arrogance" in a system of speech named for this word that was often used in a type of prison called a bagnio ("BAN-yo").

swap.text: This king's reign saw the disastrous Second Crusade and the beginning of the feud between France and England. More positively, his reign saw the beginning of the construction of the Notre-Dame de Paris.
swap.answerHtml: <u>Louis VII</u> of France [or <u>Louis the Young</u> (er) or <u>Louis le jeune</u>]
swap.clue: The cathedral at St. Denis was constructed during the reign of this monarch under the supervision of the Abbot Suger.

question.leadin: This ruler's descendants divided up his territory in the Treaty of Verdun ("ver-DUN").
question.text: Name this Frankish ruler who was crowned Emperor by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day, 800 CE.
question.clue: The Saxon Wars waged by this ruler were partially prompted by his massacre of 4,500 prisoners at Verden.

swap.leadin: He appointed Benedict of Aniane to reform the Frankish Church.
swap.text: Name this King of Aquitaine, whose sons Lothair, Louis, and Pepin fought a civil war before agreeing to divide the empire in the Treaty of Verdun.
swap.answerHtml: Louis the Pious (accept Louis the Fair, Louis the Debonaire, or Louis I; prompt on “Louis”)
swap.clue: He was briefly revolted against by his librarian Ebbo, the Archbishop of Reims, who propped up this man's son Pepin of Aquitaine.

question.text: Name this 1805 victory, largely considered his greatest, in which Napoleon hid his elite troops in the fog to surprise and destroy a joint Austrian and Russian army under Francis II and Alexander I respectively.
question.clue: During this battle the St. Hilaire's Division alongside the IV Corps of Marshal Soult led an assault on the Pratzen Heights, where earlier Mikhail Kutuzov was forced to abandon his position.

swap.leadin: Despite proclaiming that "Empire means peace," this man pursued an aggressive foreign policy which recaptured the Papal States for Pope Pius IX.
swap.text: Name this French leader who also tried to install Maximilian I as Emperor of Mexico. His reign ended with a defeat at the hands of the Prussians at the Battle of Sedan.
swap.answerHtml: Napoleon III [or Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte; do not prompt “Napoleon” or “Bonaparte”]
swap.clue: The heavy cost of victories at Magenta and Solferino led this man to hastily conclude the Armistice of Villafranca with Austria.

question.leadin: A corps of English royalists under the future James II fought at this battle, but lost despite the success of the Prince of Conde's cavalry.
question.text: Name this 1658 battle in which elements of the New Model army under Sir William Lockhart reinforced the French under the Vicomte de Turenne and forced the Peace of the Pyrenees by defeating the Spanish.
question.clue: This battle, which was fought near the Furnes canal, featured a charge by the left side of the winning forces led by William Lockhart, while the losing side's left flank was led by a French rebel, the Prince de Conde.

swap.text: Sentenced to life imprisonment on Devil's Island, Emile Zola's article "J'accuse" was instrumental in swaying public opinion and gaining his release. For fifteen points, name the Jewish French army captain falsely convicted for betraying French secrets in the late 19th century.
swap.clue: The newspaper La Libre Parole frequently attacked this person based on documents that included a "bordereau" discovered in a wastebasket.

question.text: The law legalizing abortion in France is named for this Minister of Health, a Holocaust survivor who also served as the first President of the European Parliament.

swap.leadin: A village inhabited by members of this group is the subject of an influential microhistory by Emmanuel Le Roy Ladurie.
swap.text: Name these Occitan heretics, based in Southern France, who were massacred at Beziers during an early 13th-century crusade led by Simon de Montfort the Elder.
swap.clue: The elder Simon de Montfort died in a campaign against this group which greatly reduced the political independence of Languedoc and saw a massacre in which Arnaud Amalric reportedly said "Kill them. For the Lord knows those that are His own."

question.leadin: Descendants of this king include Leopold II of Belgium, Queen Mercedes of Spain, and Empress Carlota of Mexico.
question.text: Name this penultimate king of France who took power following the July Revolution. Perhaps ironically, in his youth this king fought in the French Revolution.
question.clue: This ruler was caricatured as Gargantua in a lithograph by Honore Daumier ("ON-o-ray daw-mya").

swap.text: This moderate leftist leader became Prime Minister after the 1936 French general election. He was denounced by Action francaise leader Xavier Vallat as a "cunning talmudist."
swap.clue: He was a follower of The Cult of the Self author Maurice Barres early in life, until they broke over the Dreyfus Affair.

question.leadin: This woman attempted to make the duke of Choiseul a new power after replacing Marie of Poland in the king's favor.
question.text: Name this tall hairstyle namesake, the most influential mistress of Louis XV.
question.answerHtml: Madame de Pompadour [or Jeanne‐Antoinette Poisson, marquise de Pompadour]
question.clue: This royal mistress, founder of a salon at Etoiles.

swap.text: If a timariot died heirless, revenue collection from his estates would be outsourced via this kind of system, in which a ruler grants the right to collect taxes as personal income to agents who paid him a fixed stream of revenue.
swap.clue: This service in which private individuals collected levies such as the taille for the French crown.

question.text: Louis the Lion, the victor at the Battle of Roche-au-Moine, was a member of this French royal house, as was his father, Philip II.

swap.text: This last battle of the Hundred Years' war saw the death of Talbot in vain pursuit of a French force that outnumbered him six to one. It arose from Bordeaux's rebellion against Charles VII in 1452.
swap.clue: In this concluding battle of the Hundred Years' War, French artillery was able to negate the English longbows. This 1453 battle resulted in England losing the territory of Gascony.

question.leadin: Name these groups that French people joined.
question.text: This fascist-Monarchist group, led by Leon Daudet and Charles Maurras, agitated against the Third Republic and groups such as Jews which it derided as "internal foreigners." It played a key role in the fall of the Daladier government in 1934.
question.clue: This formerly royalist newspaper under the direction of Charles Maurras served as the major organ of the Vichy regime.

swap.text: The French Fury was when Antwerp residents kicked the ass of this French nobleman who tried to conquer it in 1583. He might be best known for being the "frog" suitor of Elizabeth I whose attempts at marriage were discouraged by Walsingham. Name or title is acceptable.
swap.answerHtml: Francis [or Francois; or the Duke of Anjou; or the Duke of Alençon; or the Duke of Alençon, Chateau-Thierry, Anjou, Berry, and Touraine]
swap.clue: Before becoming king, the second French monarch of this name became King Consort of Scotland by marrying Mary, Queen of Scots.
